summary: This work introduces partial quantum error correction (QEC) for metrology using CSS codes, where probe states are superpositions of different code sectors and only a subset of stabilizer checks are needed to suppress noise while maintaining super-SQL scaling. The method achieves polynomial suppression $p^\delta$ (with $\delta = \lfloor(l+1)/2\rfloor$) of parallel noise and an adaptive strategy to balance performance against both parallel and perpendicular noise.
motivation: Full quantum error correction for metrology is resource-intensive; this work asks whether partial QEC suffices to preserve entanglement-enhanced sensing and protect against practical noise channels affecting probe state fidelity.
method: Probe states are encoded as superpositions of energetically distinct eigenstates of CSS codes (specifically toric codes on square/honeycomb lattices and Bacon-Shor codes). Partial error correction uses only a subset of checks; phase imprinting is $U(\theta) = e^{i\theta\sum_j S_{Z,j}}$ with weight-$l$ stabilizers, and readout via a global symmetry operator. An adaptive strategy increases stabilizer weight $l(N)$ only when perpendicular-noise QFI drops to SQL.
result: For toric codes on square lattices ($l=4$), $F_{q,Z} \propto (1-cp^2)^2 N_Z N_Z^2$ achieves super-SQL with $\delta=2$ noise suppression; for honeycomb lattices ($l=6$), $\delta=3$. The Bacon-Shor code maintains both $F_{q,X}$ and $F_{q,Z}$ above SQL up to noise strength $p < 0.09$ using adaptive weight growth, with advantage persisting to $N=10^7$ qubits despite $pN \gg 1$. Mixed $X/Z$ noise scaling: $F_{q,XZ} = F_{q,X}F_{q,Z}/(4N_Z^2)$ remains super-SQL when $\nu_X + \nu_Z > 3$.
